settings.help: While you type, the editor flags what usually causes problems: slow queries, unexpected results, or changes that affect more rows than you think. The analysis is done on the text, without querying the database. Turn off the rules that don't help you.
settings.enabled: Check the code as I write
settings.enabledHelp: Marks the problems in the margin and underlines them; hover to see why and how to fix them.
settings.loadError: Could not load the list of rules.

groups.tsql: SQL Server, Azure SQL, Fabric and Sybase

select-star.title: SELECT *
select-star.why: It fetches columns you don't use, prevents an index from covering the query, and changes shape when someone adds a column. List only the columns you need.

dml-without-where.title: UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE
dml-without-where.message: {{keyword}} without WHERE: affects all rows of the table
dml-without-where.why: Without a condition, the statement changes or deletes the whole table. If that is what you want, use TRUNCATE to empty it; otherwise, add the WHERE that limits the rows.

not-in-subquery.title: NOT IN with a subquery
not-in-subquery.message: NOT IN (subquery): if it returns a NULL, no rows come out
not-in-subquery.why: A single NULL in the subquery is enough for the condition to never be true and the query to return nothing. Use NOT EXISTS, or filter out the NULLs inside the subquery.

leading-wildcard.title: Leading wildcard
leading-wildcard.message: The pattern {{pattern}} starts with a wildcard: it can't use an index
leading-wildcard.why: A pattern that starts with % (or * / ?) forces a check of every value. If you can, anchor the start of the text ('abc%') or use a full-text search.

function-on-column.title: Function on a column in the WHERE
function-on-column.message: {{fn}}(…) on the column prevents using its index
function-on-column.why: By wrapping the column in a function, the engine has to compute it row by row. Move the transformation to the other side of the comparison (for example, a date range instead of YEAR(col) = 2024) or create an index on the expression.

equals-null.title: = NULL or <> NULL
equals-null.message: Comparing with NULL using = or <> is never true
equals-null.why: NULL is neither equal nor different to anything, not even another NULL: the condition evaluates to unknown and lets no rows through. Use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL.

order-by-ordinal.title: ORDER BY by position
order-by-ordinal.message: ORDER BY {{n}} sorts by the column's position
order-by-ordinal.why: If someone changes the order of the SELECT columns, the result is sorted by another one without warning. Write the column name or its alias.

order-by-random.title: Random order
order-by-random.message: {{call}} sorts the whole table to pick random rows
order-by-random.why: It computes a random value for each row and sorts them all, even if you then ask for just one. On large tables use the engine's sampling (TABLESAMPLE, SAMPLE) or pick from a random key range.

implicit-cross-join.title: Implicit join without a condition
implicit-cross-join.message: "{{table}}" is joined with a comma and no condition: Cartesian product
implicit-cross-join.why: A table in the FROM separated by a comma, with no WHERE condition relating it to the others, combines each row with all the others. Use JOIN … ON with the condition; if the product is intentional, write CROSS JOIN.

insert-without-columns.title: INSERT without a column list
insert-without-columns.why: Values are assigned by the position of the table's columns: if someone adds or reorders columns, the INSERT fails or stores data in the wrong column. Name the columns.

distinct-group-by.title: DISTINCT together with GROUP BY
distinct-group-by.message: DISTINCT is redundant: GROUP BY already returns unique rows
distinct-group-by.why: Grouping already leaves one row per group; DISTINCT adds work without changing the result (unless the SELECT doesn't include all the grouped columns). Remove one of the two.

union-distinct.title: UNION instead of UNION ALL
union-distinct.message: UNION removes duplicates; if there can't be any, UNION ALL is faster
union-distinct.why: UNION sorts or builds a hash of the whole result to eliminate repeated rows. If the parts don't overlap or duplicates don't matter, use UNION ALL.

nolock.title: NOLOCK / READ UNCOMMITTED
nolock.why: It can return rows that are later rolled back, duplicated rows, or missing rows if the table is reorganized during the read. If what you want is for reads not to wait, use snapshot isolation (READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT).

cursor.title: Cursors
cursor.message: Cursor: processes rows one at a time
cursor.why: A cursor walks row by row through what a set-based statement (UPDATE … FROM, MERGE, a subquery) resolves at once. If you need one, declare it LOCAL FAST_FORWARD.

set-rowcount.title: SET ROWCOUNT
set-rowcount.message: SET ROWCOUNT stays active in the session and is deprecated for INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE
set-rowcount.why: It affects all following statements in the session, including triggers, until someone sets it back to 0. Use TOP (n) in the statement.

global-identity.title: @@IDENTITY
global-identity.message: @@IDENTITY may return the identity generated by a trigger
global-identity.why: It returns the last identity value of the session in any table, even one inserted by a trigger. Use SCOPE_IDENTITY() or the OUTPUT clause.

sp-prefix.title: Procedures with the sp_ prefix
sp-prefix.message: "{{name}}": the sp_ prefix is for system procedures
sp-prefix.why: SQL Server looks for sp_ procedures in master first, which costs an extra lookup on every call and may run a system one with the same name. Use another prefix (usp_) or none.

set-nocount.title: Procedure without SET NOCOUNT ON
set-nocount.why: Without it, each statement sends the client an "N rows affected" message: extra traffic and, for some clients, unexpected results. Add SET NOCOUNT ON at the start of the body.

for-update-wait.title: FOR UPDATE that waits for the lock
for-update-wait.message: {{clause}} waits for the lock to be released
for-update-wait.why: If another transaction holds the row, the query waits. For work queues use SKIP LOCKED; to fail right away, NOWAIT (in Oracle also WAIT n).

serial-identity.title: serial instead of IDENTITY
serial-identity.why: serial creates a separate sequence that doesn't travel with the permissions or with copies of the table and lets you insert values by hand without control. IDENTITY columns are the SQL standard and the sequence stays bound to the column.

group-by-nonaggregated.title: Columns outside the GROUP BY
group-by-nonaggregated.message: "{{column}}" is neither grouped nor inside an aggregate function
group-by-nonaggregated.why: MySQL without ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY returns the value of an arbitrary row of the group, and with that mode the query fails. Add the column to the GROUP BY or use an aggregate function (MAX, ANY_VALUE…).

rownum-order-by.title: ROWNUM with ORDER BY
rownum-order-by.message: ROWNUM is applied before ORDER BY
rownum-order-by.why: In the same block, Oracle numbers and cuts the rows before sorting them: it doesn't return "the first N" according to the order. Sort in a subquery and filter ROWNUM outside, or use FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY.

outer-join-plus.title: (+) outer join syntax
outer-join-plus.message: (+) is the old outer join syntax
outer-join-plus.why: It has restrictions that LEFT/RIGHT JOIN doesn't (it doesn't allow OR or FULL OUTER) and it is easy to forget in one of the conditions. Use LEFT JOIN … ON.

delete-without-time.title: DELETE without a time range
delete-without-time.message: DELETE without a condition on time: deletes the whole history of the series
delete-without-time.why: Without a time range, it deletes all the points that meet the condition from the beginning. Add time >= … AND time < … to limit it.

drop-series.title: DROP SERIES / MEASUREMENT
drop-series.message: DROP {{what}} deletes the whole history, with no time range
drop-series.why: It doesn't accept a time range: it removes all the points and the series index. If you want to delete a period, use DELETE with a condition on time.

allow-filtering.title: ALLOW FILTERING
allow-filtering.message: ALLOW FILTERING scans partitions to filter
allow-filtering.why: The coordinator reads data from many partitions and discards what doesn't meet the condition: the cost grows with the table. Model a table for that query or filter by the partition key.

no-partition-key.title: SELECT without a partition key
no-partition-key.message: SELECT on {{table}} without WHERE: reads all partitions
no-partition-key.why: Without restricting the partition key, the query scans the whole cluster. Filter by the partition key or paginate with token().

batch-partitions.title: BATCH across partitions
batch-partitions.message: The BATCH writes to several tables or partitions
batch-partitions.why: A batch spanning several partitions is not faster: it loads the coordinator and, if LOGGED, also writes the batch log. Use it for atomicity within a partition; to load data, send the statements separately.

write-all.title: Write without a filter
write-all.message: {{call}} has no filter: it affects everything
write-all.why: Without a filter, the operation changes or deletes all documents or keys. If that is what you want, write the explicit filter or use the engine's truncate operation; otherwise, add the condition.

where-operator.title: $where
where-operator.why: It doesn't use indexes, is slow and is disabled on many servers. Replace it with query operators or with $expr.

unanchored-regex.title: Unanchored regular expression
unanchored-regex.message: The expression {{pattern}} doesn't start with ^: it scans the whole index
unanchored-regex.why: Only an expression anchored at the start (^abc) and case-sensitive makes good use of an index. If you are searching for loose text, use a text index.

read-all.title: Read without a filter
read-all.why: It fetches all documents or keys. Add a filter, a projection and a limit to fetch only what you need.

keys-command.title: KEYS
keys-command.message: KEYS {{pattern}} scans all keys and blocks the server
keys-command.why: Redis serves one command at a time: while KEYS scans the database, it answers no one. Use SCAN with MATCH and COUNT, which advances in parts.

flush.title: FLUSHALL / FLUSHDB
flush.why: FLUSHDB empties the current database and FLUSHALL all the databases on the server, with no way back. Make sure you are connected to the right server.

big-read.title: Full read of a key
big-read.why: With large keys, the response takes long and blocks the server while it is built. Use HSCAN / SSCAN, or ask for a bounded range.

match-without-label.title: MATCH without a label
match-without-label.message: This pattern has no label or properties: it scans all nodes
match-without-label.why: Without a label (:Person) or a property filter, the engine has to check every node in the database. Add the label so it can use its indexes.

cartesian-product.title: Disconnected patterns
cartesian-product.message: This pattern shares no nodes with the rest: Cartesian product
cartesian-product.why: Two patterns separated by a comma with no variables in common combine each result of one with all those of the other. Relate them in the same pattern or with a WHERE.

detach-delete-all.title: DETACH DELETE without WHERE
detach-delete-all.message: DETACH DELETE without WHERE deletes all the nodes the MATCH finds
detach-delete-all.why: It deletes the nodes and all their relationships. Without a WHERE or a property filter, it takes all the nodes of the pattern with it. Review the MATCH; to delete many, do it in batches (CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS).
